variants.title: Server 1 is overloaded
variants.context: Three app servers are live, but 90% of traffic still routes to Server 1.
variants.constraint: The other servers are almost idle.
variants.question: What is the root cause?
variants.expectedPattern: Clients are bypassing a distribution layer and hitting one server directly.

variants.title: One server dies
variants.context: An instance fails in the middle of a traffic burst and requests start failing immediately.
variants.constraint: The remaining servers are healthy but not all traffic is rerouted.
variants.question: How do you route around the failure?
variants.expectedPattern: Add a load balancer with health checks that remove unhealthy nodes from rotation.
wrongChoices: Keep sending requests to the dead node

variants.title: Mobile clients bypass the public endpoint
variants.context: The app has two servers, but mobile traffic is still pointed at the old host directly.
variants.constraint: The app layer is horizontally scaled but not reachable through the load balancer.
variants.question: What completes the fix?
variants.expectedPattern: Send all traffic through the load balancer so distribution is centralized.

variants.title: Uneven traffic after a deployment
variants.context: A new version is deployed to two servers, but one receives 68% of the traffic.
variants.constraint: The balancing policy is not consistent and one node gets more than its share.
variants.question: What is the immediate design problem?
variants.expectedPattern: The routing policy is not distributing work evenly.

variants.title: Latency climbs after an app restart
variants.context: One app server is restarted and the traffic is still mostly directed to the old instance.
variants.constraint: Healthy nodes are available but get little traffic.
variants.question: What keeps the system unhealthy?
variants.expectedPattern: Long-lived client-targeting or stale routing still bypasses the balancing layer.

variants.title: All traffic hits one edge instance
variants.context: A single edge service is the main public door, but the remaining edges are not in rotation.
variants.constraint: The app is scaled yet not balanced.
variants.question: What is the best fix?
variants.expectedPattern: Use a reverse proxy or load balancer with health checks and failover.
wrongChoices: Use only round robin without health checks

variants.title: A region fails but no traffic shift happens
variants.context: A regional app server crashes, yet clients continue hitting the bad endpoint for a long time.
variants.constraint: There is a health check gap.
variants.question: Which property should the distribution layer provide?
variants.expectedPattern: Automatic removal of unhealthy targets from the rotation and rerouting.

variants.title: Traffic spins between two servers
variants.context: A two-node system alternates latency spikes even though the nodes are healthy.
variants.constraint: The routing algorithm is not aware of node health and session stickiness is weak.
variants.question: What should be improved?
variants.expectedPattern: Session-aware or health-aware balancing plus better backend utilization.

variants.title: Cascading failures after one crash
variants.context: During a moderate surge, one node dies and the rest absorb too much traffic until they also fail.
variants.constraint: The load balancer had no failover policy for partial failure.
variants.question: What design decision prevents this pattern?
variants.expectedPattern: Keep capacity above normal load and remove failed nodes aggressively.

variants.title: Traffic is uneven by geography
variants.context: Users in Europe are routed to one node while Asia goes to another, and one node is overloaded.
variants.constraint: The balancing layer is not aware of region or health.
variants.question: What is the correct balancing principle?
variants.expectedPattern: Balance by health and capacity, not simply by static rules or manual assignment.

variants.title: gRPC clients pin to one pod
variants.context: A gRPC client pool opens long-lived connections and 80% of RPCs stay on the first pod.
variants.constraint: The balancer only sees connection count, not RPC rate.
variants.question: What restores even RPC distribution?
variants.expectedPattern: Balance at request level or refresh backends so long-lived connections do not pin load.

variants.title: Health checks pass on a dying node
variants.context: A node answers /health in 5ms but its request queue is 12 seconds deep.
variants.constraint: The probe does not measure real work capacity.
variants.question: What should the balancer use instead?
variants.expectedPattern: Health checks that include queue depth, error rate, or dependency readiness.
wrongChoices: Route extra traffic to that node to test it

variants.title: Canary takes all production traffic
variants.context: A 5% canary is deployed, but weighted routing is misconfigured and the canary receives 100%.
variants.constraint: The canary has far less capacity than the stable pool.
variants.question: What did the balancing layer fail to do?
variants.expectedPattern: Honor traffic weights so only a small share reaches the canary.
wrongChoices: Increase canary CPU after the spike
Use DNS round robin as the only control

variants.title: Least-connections prefers a slow node
variants.context: A slow instance holds connections longer, so least-connections keeps sending it more work.
variants.constraint: Connection count is a poor proxy for remaining capacity.
variants.question: How should routing adapt?
variants.expectedPattern: Use latency-aware or utilization-aware balancing, not connection count alone.

variants.title: Internal services skip the mesh
variants.context: Public traffic is balanced, but service-to-service calls go to hardcoded IPs.
variants.constraint: One internal host becomes a hidden hotspot.
variants.question: What completes the architecture?
variants.expectedPattern: Send east-west traffic through a balancer or service mesh with health-aware routing.
wrongChoices: Hardcode a second IP in every client
Add a CDN in front of internal RPCs

variants.title: Draining a node still receives writes
variants.context: An instance is marked for deploy, but new requests keep landing on it until it is killed.
variants.constraint: The balancer has no connection-drain or weight-zero path.
variants.question: What should happen before shutdown?
variants.expectedPattern: Take the node out of rotation, drain in-flight work, then stop the process.
wrongChoices: Wait for users to stop clicking

variants.title: Layer-4 balancer hides HTTP errors
variants.context: TCP health checks stay green while the app returns 503 on every request.
variants.constraint: The balancer only knows the port is open.
variants.question: What check is missing?
variants.expectedPattern: Application-level health checks that fail when the service cannot serve correctly.

variants.title: Sticky sessions after node loss
variants.context: A node dies and users bound to it get errors until their sticky cookie expires.
variants.constraint: Affinity outlives the backend.
variants.question: How should the balancer behave?
variants.expectedPattern: Drop affinity for dead targets and reassign those users to healthy nodes.
wrongChoices: Keep sending them to the dead node
Force all users onto one remaining node forever

variants.title: Burst of retries overwhelms survivors
variants.context: Clients retry failed calls and the remaining two nodes receive 3x traffic instantly.
variants.constraint: The balancer has no retry budget or overload shed.
variants.question: What protection belongs at the distribution layer?
variants.expectedPattern: Shed load, cap retries, and keep enough healthy capacity before amplifying traffic.
wrongChoices: Retry every failure immediately with no cap

variants.title: Anycast edge sends all packets to one PoP
variants.context: An Anycast VIP is announced from three PoPs, but one PoP attracts almost all users.
variants.constraint: Routing is based on BGP, not backend health.
variants.question: What should you add behind the VIP?
variants.expectedPattern: Local load balancing with health checks inside each PoP, plus withdraw unhealthy announcements.
wrongChoices: A single origin database in that PoP
Manual user assignment by country code only
Longer TCP timeouts at the busy PoP
